title: OpenAI Agents approval-aware evidence
nextDecision: Decide whether to run a bounded local spike after the next radar review.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Recorded AIM and Git observations without provider approval lifecycle metadata
capabilityDelta.candidate: Preserve handoffs, guardrails, approvals, interruptions and resumed attempts as evidence
capabilityDelta.alternative: Discard provider lifecycle metadata and analyze only completed tool calls
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Identity and approval-state retention across pause/resume fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: A tool call requiring approval, rejection and later resumption

hypothesis.statement: Approval-aware mapping can reduce unknown lifecycle states without creating false independent-candidate classifications
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The mapping loses attempt ownership or produces a stronger classification than the input evidence supports

evidencePlan: Build synthetic pause, approve, reject and resume records
Compare retained identity, effects, versions and uncertainty with the provider-neutral baseline
Record unknown rate and false-safe classifications
risks: Approval metadata may contain sensitive arguments
Tracing does not prove execution authorization
limits: No adapter correctness or market superiority is established

title: MCP asynchronous task and state analysis
nextDecision: Decide whether a pinned MCP task version and synthetic fixture are available for a spike.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Tool-call evidence without a portable lifecycle for deferred results
capabilityDelta.candidate: Preserve task IDs, status, TTL, protocol version and explicit state handles
capabilityDelta.alternative: Flatten each deferred call into an unversioned completed operation
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Task/state identity and version retention across polling fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: A task transitions from working to failed or completed while the caller resumes

hypothesis.statement: Explicit task and state metadata can improve provenance coverage for asynchronous operations while preserving unknown on unsupported semantics
hypothesis.invalidationResult: Flattening or protocol-version ambiguity causes a stronger result than the source permits

evidencePlan: Create synthetic tasks/get, task result and state-handle records
Check identity, version, dependency and effect preservation
Measure unknown classifications for unsupported task extensions
risks: MCP proposals and SDK support may differ
State handles can expose sensitive context
Protocol conformance is not semantic independence
limits: No MCP runtime or SDK is installed
The track does not adopt a protocol version

title: A2A conformance-backed task evidence
nextDecision: Reassess after a versioned A2A conformance artifact is selected.

capabilityDelta.baseline: No cross-agent protocol adapter in the current analyzer
capabilityDelta.candidate: Retain task timelines, artifacts, streaming events and conformance metadata in AIM evidence
capabilityDelta.alternative: Treat remote agent messages as opaque unstructured text
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Preserved task/artifact identity and event ordering in a synthetic A2A trace
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Two agents exchange a task, artifact update and terminal event

hypothesis.statement: A conformance-backed A2A projection can make cross-agent ordering evidence inspectable without inventing independence
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The selected A2A version or TCK cannot preserve event identity and provenance

evidencePlan: Select and pin one protocol version
Use a synthetic fixture and TCK-compatible event inventory
Compare ordering and unknown behavior with a provider-neutral baseline
risks: A2A extensions and TCK are evolving
Remote artifacts may carry credentials or personal data
Interoperability does not establish semantic commutation
decisionRationale: Keep as a post-M2 candidate until a protocol version and conformance artifact are selected.
limits: No A2A adapter or conformance execution is included

title: OpenTelemetry evidence transport
nextDecision: Reassess after the monthly radar review confirms convention and privacy stability.
sourceNote: Weekly radar candidate captured on 2026-09-23; not a committed historical radar snapshot.

capabilityDelta.baseline: No generic trace transport for external agent and tool observations
capabilityDelta.candidate: Ingest optional spans and events while preserving source boundaries and redaction
capabilityDelta.alternative: Require provider-specific trace parsers or capture raw prompt content
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Identity/effect retention and redaction rate on synthetic traces
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: An agent span contains model, tool and token metadata with sensitive content disabled

hypothesis.statement: A vendor-neutral trace bridge can broaden evidence ingestion without making experimental telemetry conventions normative
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The bridge requires sensitive content, loses provenance or raises assurance without stable conventions

evidencePlan: Measure retained fields, redactions and unknown rate
risks: Trace payloads can contain secrets or personal data
Telemetry is observation, not execution authorization
decisionRationale: Observe convention stability and privacy requirements before a spike.
limits: No OpenTelemetry dependency or collector is introduced

title: CoAgent/MTPO research comparator
nextDecision: Decide whether an artifact-level reproduction is feasible at M2.

capabilityDelta.baseline: Agent Braid bounded Git and AIM analysis with no runtime transaction protocol
capabilityDelta.candidate: Compare advisory serialization, repair and undo assumptions against Agent Braid's evidence model
capabilityDelta.alternative: Treat the paper's reported metrics as direct proof of a better algorithm
capabilityDelta.observableMetric: Reproduced semantics, workload coverage, unknown behavior and cost under matched fixtures
capabilityDelta.comparisonScenario: Shared-state agent operations with declared footprints and a conflicting write

hypothesis.statement: A bounded semantic comparison can identify complementary or contradictory assumptions without adopting the paper's runtime protocol
hypothesis.invalidationResult: The artifact or semantics cannot be reproduced sufficiently to support a fair comparison

evidencePlan: Obtain and inspect the authors' artifact if available
Map assumptions to AIM and operational semantics
Report positive, negative or inconclusive reproduction separately
risks: The source is an unreproduced preprint
Runtime assumptions differ from Agent Braid's read-only boundary
Throughput comparisons may double-count incompatible workloads
decisionRationale: Keep as an M2 scientific comparator; do not incorporate MTPO into the scheduler.
limits: No reproduction or algorithm adoption is included
